description: Renovate keeps the sha256-pinned release downloads in the workflows current (gitleaks,
actionlint, osv-scanner, the Codacy coverage reporter), which Dependabot cannot see, and the
container images pinned as tag@sha256: the fuzz image's base (.clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile), the
images of this repository's two ClusterFuzzLite actions (.github/actions/cflite-*/action.yml) and
the Scorecard action's image recorded in scorecard.yml. For an image it proposes the tag's new
digest when the tag moves, never another tag: the Scorecard tag follows the action's version,
which Dependabot updates.
Everything else stays with Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml, which has no docker entry), so
the two never propose the same update: the github-actions manager reads the two local action
files only, never a workflow.
Each pinned download is marked in its step's env with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=owner/repo`
line directly above the VERSION (the release tag) and SHA256 lines. The
github-release-attachments datasource finds the asset the current sha256 belongs to and
proposes the new tag together with that asset's new sha256. A pinned image in a workflow is an
*IMAGE: 'name:tag@sha256:...' line under `# renovate: datasource=docker`.
The registries these images live on (gcr.io, ghcr.io) give Renovate no release timestamp, and
with the default timestamp-required a digest update would wait on minimumReleaseAge forever, so
docker updates are raised without one (Renovate docs, minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour).
tests/unit/part19.py and part242.py gate that every pin is matched and that each manager reads
only its own files.
